      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object

          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1

          type: string
          minLength: 1

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'

          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison

## Summary

I added optional `email` support to owners, validated and lower-cased through the OfficeFloor function pipeline (not a Spring controller), following the project's existing telephone-handling pattern.

**Model & schema**
- `Owner.java` — added a nullable `email` field (`@Column(name = "email")`) with getter/setter.
- `openapi.yml` — added an optional `email` property to the `OwnerFields` schema (plain string, `maxLength: 255`, not in `required`), so the generated DTO carries it and MapStruct maps it by name.
- DB schemas (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added an `email VARCHAR(255)`/`TEXT` column.
- `hsqldb/data.sql` — the seed used positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)`, which breaks when a column is added, so I gave those 10 inserts explicit column lists (h2/postgres already used explicit columns).

**Pipeline (function injection)**
- New `NormalizeOwnerEmail` step: absent/blank email is left alone; a present value is syntactically validated (regex) and stored back lower-cased; an invalid value throws the checked `InvalidEmailException`.
- New `InvalidEmailException` + `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler` and its `officefloor/escalation/...InvalidEmailException.yml`, responding **400** with a `ProblemDetail` — mirroring the telephone escalation.
- Wired the `normalizeEmail` step into `owners.POST.yml` (after build) and `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` (after apply), under the same `transaction` governance.
- `ApplyOwner` now also copies `email` from the request so updates flow through.

The three acceptance tests — lower-casing `Test.User@Example.COM` → `test.user@example.com`, rejecting `not-an-email` with 400, and accepting a missing email — all pass.

Note: the repo isn't a git repository, so I made no commit. Let me know if you'd like me to `git init` and commit.
